concepts.name: Merge vs. Separate Deployment
concepts.summary: A trained LoRA pair A, B has two deployments. MERGE folds it in: W_merged = W + B.A, a single matrix with zero extra inference cost but W permanently changed. KEEP SEPARATE ships W untouched plus tiny A, B and computes the branch live, y = W.x + (B.A.x).alpha (the ComfyUI plug-in case). The pair always exists after training; merging is optional. This resolves the confusion between 'fine-tuning updates W' (merged) and 'download a LoRA and plug it in' (separate).

concepts.name: Stacking & Scaling Adapters
concepts.summary: Because each LoRA branch is just an addition onto W.x, kept-separate adapters can be swapped, stacked, and scaled. Stack: y = W.x + B1A1x + B2A2x + ... (style + character + pose). Scale: each branch has its own alpha strength dial (the ComfyUI slider; 0 = off, 1 = trained strength, >1 = stronger). The base checkpoint W is multi-GB downloaded once; LoRA files are 10-200 MB downloaded many. Merging forfeits all three freedoms for one fast matrix.

concepts.name: The PEFT Workflow
concepts.summary: Forging a LoRA in code is four moves: (1) load the frozen base; (2) define a LoraConfig with r, lora_alpha, and target_modules (typically attention q_proj/k_proj/v_proj/o_proj); (3) get_peft_model() injects the parallel A, B branches and freezes the rest; (4) train normally so only A, B get gradients. save_pretrained writes just the few-MB adapter; PeftModel.from_pretrained plugs it back; merge_and_unload folds it in. diffusers follows the same moves for U-Net attention (to_q/to_k/to_v/to_out.0).

concepts.name: QLoRA
concepts.summary: QLoRA loads the frozen base in 4-bit quantization and trains the LoRA on top in full precision. The base is only read in the forward pass (never receives a gradient), so a coarse 4-bit copy suffices for W.x, while the tiny trainable A, B stay full precision. This cuts memory ~4x (the base is nearly all of it), letting large models be fine-tuned on a single consumer GPU. Enabled via BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True, ...) then the usual get_peft_model().
